newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy wants good ties with new Zaire government.
newsitem.headline: Italy wants good ties with new Zaire government.

text.p: Italy said on Monday it intended to establish a "constructive relationship" with Kinshasa and urged the new authorities to guarantee assistance to refugees and allow aid agencies to carry out their work.
In a statement, the foreign ministry referred throughout to the "Congolese authorities" rather than Zaire.
Following a seven-month civil war in Zaire, self-proclaimed president Laurent Kabila on Saturday changed the name of the country to the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Zaire President Mobutu Sese Seko relinquished power and abandoned his capital the previous day.

"The Italian government, in noting the recent political and institutional changes that have taken place in Kinshasa, intends to establish a constructive relationship with the new Congolese authorities and the government that will be established," the foreign ministry statement said.

"Italy hopes that the new Kinshasa government can be built on a broad base and will lead to the political-institutional and economic rebuilding of the country on democratic principles and the respect for human rights," it said.
It said Italy promised to make its own contribution, both bilaterally and through the European Union.

"The Italian government takes the opportunity to appeal to the new Congolese authorities to guarantee assistance to refugees and allow humanitarian organisations to carry out their tasks," the statement said.

Hundreds of thousands of Rwandan Hutu refugees are sheltering in the country after fleeing their homeland in 1994 to escape reprisals for the genocide of up to 800,000 Tutsis and moderate Hutus. A huge area of eastern Zaire has remained off-limits to aid workers.
